CalibrationMath

class CalibrationMath[source]

Bases: object

Mathematical utilities for projection / keystone calibration.

All methods are classmethods; the class holds no state.

Notes

Corner points are always ordered top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right (TL, TR, BL, BR), both in the source rectangle of get_perspective_transform and in the destination points.

Methods

calculate_centered_destination_points

Compute the corners of the content area on the screen.

calculate_destination_points_with_flip

Compute the content corners with optional mirroring.

calculate_projection_area

Compute the content size that fits the screen at a ratio.

get_inverse_transform

Return the inverse of a transform matrix.

get_perspective_transform

Build the 3x3 homography from content to destination points.
classmethod calculate_projection_area(screen_width, screen_height, aspect_ratio)[source]

Compute the content size that fits the screen at a ratio.

Parameters:
screen_widthint

Screen width in pixels.

screen_heightint

Screen height in pixels.

aspect_ratiotuple[int, int]

Desired width/height ratio, e.g. (4, 3) or (16, 9).

Returns:
tuple[int, int]

(content_width, content_height) in pixels.

Raises:
ValueError

If aspect_ratio is not a tuple of two positive values.

Notes

Height has priority: the content takes the full screen height and the width follows the ratio. Only when that width exceeds the screen width is the content fitted to the full width instead. Integer division is used, so sizes are rounded down.

Examples

>>> calc = CalibrationMath.calculate_projection_area
>>> calc(1920, 1080, (4, 3))
(1440, 1080)
>>> calc(1280, 1024, (16, 9))
(1280, 720)
classmethod calculate_centered_destination_points(screen_width, screen_height, content_width, content_height, center_horizontally=True, center_vertically=True)[source]

Compute the corners of the content area on the screen.

Parameters:
screen_widthint

Screen width in pixels.

screen_heightint

Screen height in pixels.

content_widthint

Content width in pixels.

content_heightint

Content height in pixels.

center_horizontallybool, optional

Center the content horizontally; otherwise align it to the left edge. Default is True.

center_verticallybool, optional

Center the content vertically; otherwise align it to the top edge. Default is True.

Returns:
numpy.ndarray

float32 array of shape (4, 2) with the (x, y) corners in TL, TR, BL, BR order.

Examples

>>> pts = CalibrationMath.calculate_centered_destination_points(
...     1920, 1080, 1440, 1080
... )
>>> pts.tolist()
[[240.0, 0.0], [1680.0, 0.0], [240.0, 1080.0], [1680.0, 1080.0]]
classmethod calculate_destination_points_with_flip(screen_width, screen_height, content_width, content_height, flip_h=False, flip_v=False, center_horizontally=True, center_vertically=True)[source]

Compute the content corners with optional mirroring.

Parameters:
screen_widthint

Screen width in pixels.

screen_heightint

Screen height in pixels.

content_widthint

Content width in pixels.

content_heightint

Content height in pixels.

flip_hbool, optional

Mirror the content horizontally. Default is False.

flip_vbool, optional

Mirror the content vertically. Default is False.

center_horizontallybool, optional

Center the content horizontally. Default is True.

center_verticallybool, optional

Center the content vertically. Default is True.

Returns:
numpy.ndarray

float32 array of shape (4, 2) with the corners of calculate_centered_destination_points reordered for the requested mirroring.

Notes

Mirroring only reorders the corners (TL, TR, BL, BR = 0, 1, 2, 3): horizontal uses [1, 0, 3, 2], vertical [2, 3, 0, 1] and both [3, 2, 1, 0]. Used as destination points of get_perspective_transform, this flips the warped image.

Examples

>>> cm = CalibrationMath
>>> pts = cm.calculate_destination_points_with_flip(
...     100, 50, 100, 50, flip_h=True
... )
>>> pts.tolist()
[[100.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0], [100.0, 50.0], [0.0, 50.0]]
classmethod get_perspective_transform(content_size, dst_points)[source]

Build the 3x3 homography from content to destination points.

Parameters:
content_sizetuple[int, int]

(width, height) of the source content in pixels.

dst_pointsnumpy.ndarray

float32 array of shape (4, 2) with the destination corners in TL, TR, BL, BR order.

Returns:
numpy.ndarray

3x3 perspective matrix from cv2.getPerspectiveTransform.

Examples

>>> import numpy as np
>>> dst = np.float32([[0, 0], [100, 0], [0, 50], [100, 50]])
>>> calc = CalibrationMath.get_perspective_transform
>>> m = calc((100, 50), dst)
>>> bool(np.allclose(m, np.eye(3)))
True
classmethod get_inverse_transform(matrix)[source]

Return the inverse of a transform matrix.

Used to map screen/camera points back to game coordinates.

Parameters:
matrixnumpy.ndarray

Square transform matrix, usually from get_perspective_transform.

Returns:
numpy.ndarray

Inverse matrix computed by numpy.linalg.inv.

Raises:
numpy.linalg.LinAlgError

If the matrix is singular.

Examples

>>> import numpy as np
>>> m = np.array([[2.0, 0, 0], [0, 2.0, 0], [0, 0, 1.0]])
>>> CalibrationMath.get_inverse_transform(m).diagonal().tolist()
[0.5, 0.5, 1.0]
